answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: Anthony wrote this in a spring 1893 fund-raising appeal printed in the Woman’s Tribune and reproduced verbatim in her authorized biography, Ida Husted Harper’s Life and Work of Susan B. Anthony, Vol. 2 (1898). The familiar one-line version simply drops her closing words, “…from this to the day of the election.”

source.excerpt: … we must organize every school district of every county of each State in which the battle of the ballot for woman is to be fought. Organize, agitate, educate, must be our war cry from this to the day of the election.
trail: The line appears verbatim in Ida Husted Harper’s Life and Work of Susan B. Anthony, Vol. 2 (1898), Ch. XLI, quoting Anthony’s spring 1893 appeal to the Woman’s Tribune.
Notably, Wikiquote’s Anthony page omits the line altogether — yet the primary text confirms it is genuine.
Quote sites such as Women on 20s circulate the tidied one-line form with no source attached.
It should not be confused with the older, reversed-order socialist slogan “Educate! Agitate! Organise!” (Social Democratic Federation, 1883).
source.excerptNote: From Anthony’s spring 1893 appeal in the Woman’s Tribune, urging supporters to fund the Colorado, Kansas and New York campaigns.

author.name: Susan B. Anthony
author.heading: About Susan B. Anthony
author.bio: Susan B. Anthony was the tireless organizer of the American woman-suffrage movement, co-founder (with Elizabeth Cady Stanton) of the National Woman Suffrage Association, and co-author of the multi-volume History of Woman Suffrage. Arrested in 1872 for voting, she spent the next three decades crisscrossing the country raising money and campaigning state by state. She died in 1906, fourteen years before the Nineteenth Amendment enshrined the vote she never got to cast legally.

misattribution.heading: Genuine — but often tidied
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Anthony is correct. Two smaller things get muddled, though:

items.why: The popular form drops Anthony’s closing words, “…from this to the day of the election,” turning a campaign-specific rallying cry into a timeless maxim. The primary text shows the full sentence.

items.who: British socialists & later B. R. Ambedkar
items.why: The reversed-order slogan “Educate! Agitate! Organise!” traces to the Social Democratic Federation’s 1883 pamphlet Socialism Made Plain — a separate lineage from Anthony’s suffrage “war cry.”

misattribution.truthLine: Anthony really wrote “Organize, agitate, educate, must be our war cry” — in a spring 1893 fund-raising appeal to the Woman’s Tribune, reproduced in her authorized biography.

context.heading: Why she said it
lead: In the spring of 1893 Anthony was seventy-three and driving three simultaneous state suffrage campaigns — Colorado, Kansas and New York. The “war cry” was, quite literally, a plea for cash: printed in the Woman’s Tribune, it begged supporters to send money so organizers could reach “every school district of every county” before the ballots were cast.
The appeal worked where it mattered most: that November, Colorado’s male voters approved woman suffrage by popular referendum — the first state ever to do so at the ballot box.
detailsBody: Anthony’s letter closes: “Do let us all take to ourselves new hope and courage for the herculean task before us. Who will send the next $100? O, that we had $10,000 to start with!”
